name: bm-e3-closed-3d-lumenoid
title: Closed 3D lumenoid morphogenesis
claim: A closed lumenoid with a lumen pressure and a basal membrane surface runs the vertex model; attaching an explicit membrane and reading curvature-dependent shape is next.
question: How do lumen pressure/volume and a basement-membrane shell set cell shape and curvature- dependent growth in a closed 3D lumenoid?
hypothesis: A closed curved Tyssue epithelium with a lumen volume/pressure constraint and a BM shell predicts lumen growth and curvature-dependent cell shapes that depend on BM relaxation, first with a validated reduced-order BM law and then with resolved LAMMPS patches or a curved-network realization.
objective: Introduce a 3D closed-shell Tyssue geometry with lumen pressure/volume and a BM shell; first use the validated reduced-order BM law, then test resolved LAMMPS patches or a curved- network realization; predict lumen growth, cell shape and curvature effects.
description:
The closed lumenoid extension (plan section 5, 3D lumenoid level). A closed curved
epithelium with lumen volume/pressure and a BM shell is the full morphogenesis target. The
reduced-order BM law (validated in R4-R5) is used first; resolved LAMMPS patches or a
curved-network BM are tested second. Curvature-dependent effects on lumen growth and cell
shape are the new predictions beyond the flat-substrate paper.

expected_behavior.name: lumenoid-shape-depends-on-bm
expected_behavior.condition: reduced-order BM shell vs resolved LAMMPS patch
expected_behavior.rationale: Consistency between reduced-order and resolved BM in their overlap, plus a curvature- dependent cell-shape prediction, gates the lumenoid extension (P4).

baseline.name: bm-e3-closed-3d-lumenoid
baseline.note: A closed epithelial shell of 78 cells enclosing a lumen, with the basement membrane as its outer basal surface. The model carries a lumen pressure that grows as the lumen fills, and it exposes that basal surface as the membrane the collagen network attaches to. The membrane is treated first as an effective material; a collagen patch resolved at the molecular scale comes later.
